newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. STOCKS SEEN HIGHER AFTER DATA.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. STOCKS SEEN HIGHER AFTER DATA.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening higher on Wednesday in reaction to July retail sales and wholesale price data, analysts said. The following are their comments:

GUY TRUICKO, PORTFOLIO MANAGER, UNITY MANAGEMENT: Said the data is better than expect. "Bonds are rallying on the news...I would think (stocks will open) positive, the way stocks have been following bonds. We should look for a higher opening."

The government reported the July Producer Price Index fell 0.1 percent overall, and 0.1 percent without the volatile food and energy components. Economists had expected, on average, the index to rise 0.1 percent in the overall and core numbers.
July retail sares rose 0.6 percent overall and 0.5 percent excluding autos. Economists had expected an overall rise of 0.7 percent and 0.5 percent ex-autos.

ALAN ACKERMAN, MARKET STRATEGIST AT FAHNESTOCK & CO: "A sense of relief has suddenly covered the bond market. It's reassuring for those who were nervous about inflation. Stocks are likely to follow bonds higher."

SAM STOVALL, ANALYST AT S&P INDUSTRY REPORTS: "These numbers (both retail sales and the PPI) should be looked at very positively by markets. If they came in as expected, there would have been no surprise. But since they came in lower than expectated, we should have a very nice day in the market today. Both indicators show inflation is not a concern."
The 30-year Treasury bond was up 27/32, its yield dropping to 6.60 percent from Tuesday's close at 6.67 percent.
